question: Why does canned stout need a rattling plastic capsule inside to pour with a thick, creamy head?
answer: Because its foam relies on nitrogen, which barely dissolves in beer. The capsule fills with gas and beer under pressure at canning; when the can opens, pressure drops and it squirts a jet through a tiny hole, releasing bubbles at once. A pub tap does the same, forcing stout through a plate of fine holes.
move: When something will not start on its own, give it a place to begin.
source: Bamforth, Beer: Tap into the Art and Science
reference: Bamforth, Beer: Tap into the Art and Science of Brewing, 3rd edition, Oxford University Press, 2009
